audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 16, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal witness, archaeological, and reception-history audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for dynastic curse, corpse exposure, alcohol context, assassination, household extermination, seven-day rule, siege, Zimri's self-inflicted death by fire, civil conflict, Samaria land purchase, Ahab and Jezebel, anti-foreign-wife scapegoating, religious persecution risk, and deaths of Hiel's sons.

verses.restored: Word of YHWH came to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha, saying:

familiar.text: Then the word of the LORD came to Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha, saying,

modern.text: Then the word of the LORD came to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha, saying:

original.text: וַיְהִ֤י דְבַר יְהוָה֙ אֶל יֵה֣וּא בֶן חֲנָ֔נִי עַל בַּעְשָׁ֖א לֵאמֹֽר

verses.restored: Because I raised you from dust and made you leader over my people Israel, but you walked in way of Jeroboam and made my people Israel sin, provoking me with their sins,

familiar.text: Forasmuch as I exalted thee out of the dust, and made thee prince over my people Israel; and thou hast walked in the way of Jeroboam, and hast made my people Israel to sin, to provoke me to anger with their sins;

modern.text: “Even though I lifted you out of the dust and made you ruler over My people Israel, you have walked in the way of Jeroboam and have caused My people Israel to sin and to provoke Me to anger by their sins.

original.text: יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר הֲרִימֹתִ֨יךָ֙ מִן הֶ֣עָפָ֔ר וָאֶתֶּנְךָ֣ נָגִ֔יד עַ֖ל עַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַתֵּ֣לֶךְ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ יָרָבְעָ֗ם וַֽתַּחֲטִא֙ אֶת עַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְהַכְעִיסֵ֖נִי בְּחַטֹּאתָֽם

verses.restored: look, I will sweep away Baasha and his house and make your house like house of Jeroboam son of Nebat.

familiar.text: Behold, I will take away the posterity of Baasha, and the posterity of his house; and will make thy house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

modern.text: So now I will consume Baasha and his house, and I will make your house like that of Jeroboam son of Nebat:

original.text: הִנְנִ֥י מַבְעִ֛יר אַחֲרֵ֥י בַעְשָׁ֖א וְאַחֲרֵ֣י בֵית֑וֹ וְנָֽתַתִּי֙ אֶת בֵּ֣יתְךָ֔ כְּבֵ֖ית יָרָבְעָ֥ם בֶּן נְבָֽט

verses.restored: One belonging to Baasha who dies in city dogs shall eat, and one who dies in field birds of heavens shall eat.

familiar.text: Him that dieth of Baasha in the city shall the dogs eat; and him that dieth of his in the fields shall the fowls of the air eat.

modern.text: Anyone belonging to Baasha who dies in the city will be eaten by dogs, and anyone who dies in the field will be eaten by the birds of the air.”

original.text: הַמֵּ֤ת לְבַעְשָׁא֙ בָּעִ֔יר יֹֽאכְל֖וּ הַכְּלָבִ֑ים וְהַמֵּ֥ת לוֹ֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה יֹאכְל֖וּ ע֥וֹף הַשָּׁמָֽיִם

verses.restored: Rest of acts of Baasha, what he did, and his might—are they not written in book of chronicles of kings of Israel?

familiar.text: Now the rest of the acts of Baasha, and what he did, and his might, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

modern.text: As for the rest of the acts of Baasha, along with his accomplishments and might, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?

original.text: וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י בַעְשָׁ֛א וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה וּגְבֽוּרָת֑וֹ הֲלֹא הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Baasha lay with his ancestors and was buried in Tirzah. Elah his son reigned in his place.

familiar.text: So Baasha slept with his fathers, and was buried in Tirzah: and Elah his son reigned in his stead.

modern.text: And Baasha rested with his fathers and was buried in Tirzah, and his son Elah reigned in his place.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב בַּעְשָׁא֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקָּבֵ֖ר בְּתִרְצָ֑ה וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֵלָ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו

verses.restored: Also by hand of prophet Jehu son of Hanani word of YHWH came against Baasha and his house, for all evil he did in eyes of YHWH, provoking YHWH with work of his hands, becoming like house of Jeroboam, and because he killed it/him.

familiar.text: And also by the hand of the prophet Jehu the son of Hanani came the word of the LORD against Baasha, and against his house, even for all the evil that he did in the sight of the LORD, in provoking him to anger with the work of his hands, in being like the house of Jeroboam; and because he killed him.

modern.text: Moreover, the word of the LORD came through the prophet Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha and his house, because of all the evil he had done in the sight of the LORD, provoking Him to anger with the work of his hands and becoming like the house of Jeroboam, and also because Baasha had struck down the house of Jeroboam. Elah Reigns in Israel

original.text: וְגַ֡ם בְּיַד יֵה֨וּא בֶן חֲנָ֜נִי הַנָּבִ֗יא דְּבַר יְהוָ֡ה הָיָה֩ אֶל בַּעְשָׁ֨א וְאֶל בֵּית֜וֹ וְעַ֥ל כָּל הָרָעָ֣ה אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֣ה בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֗ה לְהַכְעִיסוֹ֙ בְּמַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יָדָ֔יו לִהְי֖וֹת כְּבֵ֣ית יָרָבְעָ֑ם וְעַ֥ל אֲשֶׁר הִכָּ֖ה אֹתֽוֹ

verses.restored: In twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah, Elah son of Baasha began to reign over Israel in Tirzah, two years.

familiar.text: In the twenty and sixth year of Asa king of Judah began Elah the son of Baasha to reign over Israel in Tirzah, two years.

modern.text: In the twenty-sixth year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Elah son of Baasha became king of Israel, and he reigned in Tirzah two years.

original.text: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וָשֵׁשׁ֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לְאָסָ֖א מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָ֠לַךְ אֵלָ֨ה בֶן בַּעְשָׁ֧א עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בְּתִרְצָ֖ה שְׁנָתָֽיִם

verses.restored: His servant Zimri, commander of half the chariots, conspired against him while he was in Tirzah drinking himself drunk in house of Arza, who was over household in Tirzah.

familiar.text: And his servant Zimri, captain of half his chariots, conspired against him, as he was in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza steward of his house in Tirzah.

modern.text: However, while Elah was in Tirzah getting drunk in the house of Arza the steward of his household there, Elah’s servant Zimri, the commander of half his chariots, conspired against him.

original.text: וַיִּקְשֹׁ֤ר עָלָיו֙ עַבְדּ֣וֹ זִמְרִ֔י שַׂ֖ר מַחֲצִ֣ית הָרָ֑כֶב וְה֤וּא בְתִרְצָה֙ שֹׁתֶ֣ה שִׁכּ֔וֹר בֵּ֣ית אַרְצָ֔א אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל הַבַּ֖יִת בְּתִרְצָֽה

verses.restored: Zimri came, struck him, and killed him in twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his place.

familiar.text: And Zimri went in and smote him, and killed him, in the twenty and seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his stead.

modern.text: So in the twenty-seventh year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Zimri went in, struck Elah down, and killed him. And Zimri reigned in his place.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֤א זִמְרִי֙ וַיַּכֵּ֣הוּ וַיְמִיתֵ֔הוּ בִּשְׁנַת֙ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים וָשֶׁ֔בַע לְאָסָ֖א מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּמְלֹ֖ךְ תַּחְתָּֽיו

verses.restored: When he began to reign and sat upon throne, he struck all house of Baasha. He left him no male—literally, one who urinates against wall—neither kinsman nor friend.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when he began to reign, as soon as he sat on his throne, that he slew all the house of Baasha: he left him not one that pisseth against a wall, neither of his kinsfolks, nor of his friends.

modern.text: As soon as Zimri began to reign and was seated on the throne, he struck down the entire household of Baasha. He did not leave a single male, whether a kinsman or friend.

original.text: וַיְהִ֨י בְמָלְכ֜וֹ כְּשִׁבְתּ֣וֹ עַל כִּסְא֗וֹ הִכָּה֙ אֶת כָּל בֵּ֣ית בַּעְשָׁ֔א לֹֽא הִשְׁאִ֥יר ל֖וֹ מַשְׁתִּ֣ין בְּקִ֑יר וְגֹאֲלָ֖יו וְרֵעֵֽהוּ

verses.restored: Zimri destroyed all house of Baasha according to word of YHWH spoken against Baasha by Jehu the prophet,

familiar.text: Thus did Zimri destroy all the house of Baasha, according to the word of the LORD, which he spake against Baasha by Jehu the prophet,

modern.text: So Zimri destroyed the entire household of Baasha, according to the word that the LORD had spoken against Baasha through Jehu the prophet.

original.text: וַיַּשְׁמֵ֣ד זִמְרִ֔י אֵ֖ת כָּל בֵּ֣ית בַּעְשָׁ֑א כִּדְבַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר אֶל בַּעְשָׁ֔א בְּיַ֖ד יֵה֥וּא הַנָּבִֽיא

verses.restored: for all sins of Baasha and sins of Elah his son, by which they sinned and made Israel sin, provoking YHWH, Divine of Israel, with their vanities.

familiar.text: For all the sins of Baasha, and the sins of Elah his son, by which they sinned, and by which they made Israel to sin, in provoking the LORD God of Israel to anger with their vanities.

modern.text: This happened because of all the sins Baasha and his son Elah had committed and had caused Israel to commit, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger with their worthless idols.

original.text: אֶ֚ל כָּל חַטֹּ֣אות בַּעְשָׁ֔א וְחַטֹּ֖אות אֵלָ֣ה בְנ֑וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטְא֗וּ וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר הֶחֱטִ֨יאוּ֙ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְהַכְעִ֗יס אֶת יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּהַבְלֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: Rest of acts of Elah and all he did—are they not written in book of chronicles of kings of Israel?

familiar.text: Now the rest of the acts of Elah, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

modern.text: As for the rest of the acts of Elah, along with all his accomplishments, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel? Zimri Reigns in Israel

original.text: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י אֵלָ֖ה וְכָל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלֽוֹא הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: In twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, Zimri reigned seven days in Tirzah. The people were camped against Gibbethon belonging to Philistines.

familiar.text: In the twenty and seventh year of Asa king of Judah did Zimri reign seven days in Tirzah. And the people were encamped against Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines.

modern.text: In the twenty-seventh year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Zimri reigned in Tirzah for seven days. Now the troops were encamped against Gibbethon of the Philistines,

original.text: בִּשְׁנַת֩ עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וָשֶׁ֜בַע שָׁנָ֗ה לְאָסָא֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה מָלַ֥ךְ זִמְרִ֛י שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים בְּתִרְצָ֑ה וְהָעָ֣ם חֹנִ֔ים עַֽל גִּבְּת֖וֹן אֲשֶׁ֥ר לַפְּלִשְׁתִּֽים

verses.restored: The camped people heard, Zimri conspired and also killed king. All Israel made Omri, commander of army, king over Israel that day in camp.

familiar.text: And the people that were encamped heard say, Zimri hath conspired, and hath also slain the king: wherefore all Israel made Omri, the captain of the host, king over Israel that day in the camp.

modern.text: and the people in the camp heard that Zimri had not only conspired but had also struck down the king. So there in the camp that very day, all Israel proclaimed Omri, the commander of the army, king over Israel.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע הָעָם֙ הַחֹנִ֣ים לֵאמֹ֔ר קָשַׁ֣ר זִמְרִ֔י וְגַ֖ם הִכָּ֣ה אֶת הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיַּמְלִ֣כוּ כָֽל יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל אֶת עָמְרִ֨י שַׂר צָבָ֧א עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא בַּֽמַּחֲנֶֽה

verses.restored: Omri went up from Gibbethon, and all Israel with him, and they besieged Tirzah.

familiar.text: And Omri went up from Gibbethon, and all Israel with him, and they besieged Tirzah.

modern.text: Then Omri and all the Israelites marched up from Gibbethon and besieged Tirzah.

original.text: וַיַּעֲלֶ֥ה עָמְרִ֛י וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל עִמּ֖וֹ מִֽגִּבְּת֑וֹן וַיָּצֻ֖רוּ עַל תִּרְצָֽה

verses.restored: When Zimri saw city was captured, he entered citadel of king's house, burned king's house over himself with fire, and died.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when Zimri saw that the city was taken, that he went into the palace of the king’s house, and burnt the king’s house over him with fire, and died,

modern.text: When Zimri saw that the city was captured, he entered the citadel of the royal palace and burned it down upon himself. So he died

original.text: וַיְהִ֞י כִּרְא֤וֹת זִמְרִי֙ כִּֽי נִלְכְּדָ֣ה הָעִ֔יר וַיָּבֹ֖א אֶל אַרְמ֣וֹן בֵּית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיִּשְׂרֹ֨ף עָלָ֧יו אֶת בֵּֽית מֶ֛לֶךְ בָּאֵ֖שׁ וַיָּמֹֽת

verses.restored: For sins he sinned, doing evil in eyes of YHWH, walking in way of Jeroboam and his sin by which he made Israel sin.

familiar.text: For his sins which he sinned in doing evil in the sight of the LORD, in walking in the way of Jeroboam, and in his sin which he did, to make Israel to sin.

modern.text: because of the sins he had committed, doing evil in the sight of the LORD and following the example of Jeroboam and the sin he had committed and had caused Israel to commit.

original.text: עַל חטאתו אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטָ֔א לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה לָלֶ֨כֶת֙ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ יָרָבְעָ֔ם וּבְחַטָּאתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה לְהַחֲטִ֖יא אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Rest of acts of Zimri and conspiracy he conspired—are they not written in book of chronicles of kings of Israel?

familiar.text: Now the rest of the acts of Zimri, and his treason that he wrought, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

modern.text: As for the rest of the acts of Zimri and the treason he committed, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel? Omri Reigns in Israel

original.text: וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י זִמְרִ֔י וְקִשְׁר֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר קָשָׁ֑ר הֲלֹֽא הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Then people of Israel were divided into two halves: half people followed Tibni son of Ginath to make him king, and half followed Omri.

familiar.text: Then were the people of Israel divided into two parts: half of the people followed Tibni the son of Ginath, to make him king; and half followed Omri.

modern.text: At that time the people of Israel were divided: Half of the people supported Tibni son of Ginath as king, and half supported Omri.

original.text: אָ֧ז יֵחָלֵ֛ק הָעָ֥ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לַחֵ֑צִי חֲצִ֨י הָעָ֜ם הָ֠יָה אַחֲרֵ֨י תִבְנִ֤י בֶן גִּינַת֙ לְהַמְלִיכ֔וֹ וְהַחֲצִ֖י אַחֲרֵ֥י עָמְרִֽי

verses.restored: People following Omri prevailed over people following Tibni son of Ginath. Tibni died, and Omri reigned.

familiar.text: But the people that followed Omri prevailed against the people that followed Tibni the son of Ginath: so Tibni died, and Omri reigned.

modern.text: But the followers of Omri proved stronger than those of Tibni son of Ginath. So Tibni died and Omri became king.

original.text: וַיֶּחֱזַ֤ק הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַחֲרֵ֣י עָמְרִ֔י אֶת הָעָ֕ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַחֲרֵ֖י תִּבְנִ֣י בֶן גִּינַ֑ת וַיָּ֣מָת תִּבְנִ֔י וַיִּמְלֹ֖ךְ עָמְרִֽי

verses.restored: In thirty-first year of Asa king of Judah, Omri began to reign over Israel twelve years; six years he reigned in Tirzah.

familiar.text: In the thirty and first year of Asa king of Judah began Omri to reign over Israel, twelve years: six years reigned he in Tirzah.

modern.text: In the thirty-first year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Omri became king of Israel, and he reigned twelve years, six of them in Tirzah.

original.text: בִּשְׁנַת֩ שְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים וְאַחַ֜ת שָׁנָ֗ה לְאָסָא֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה מָלַ֤ךְ עָמְרִי֙ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָ֑ה בְּתִרְצָ֖ה מָלַ֥ךְ שֵׁשׁ שָׁנִֽים

verses.restored: He bought hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver, built upon hill, and called name of city he built Samaria, after name of Shemer, owner of hill.

familiar.text: And he bought the hill Samaria of Shemer for two talents of silver, and built on the hill, and called the name of the city which he built, after the name of Shemer, owner of the hill, Samaria.

modern.text: He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver and built a city there, calling it Samaria after the name of Shemer, who had owned the hill.

translation_notes: Dynastic judgment again takes the form of household extermination and corpse exposure. These are not ethical models for political transition or accountability.
Elah is assassinated while intoxicated, but alcohol does not cause or justify Zimri's violence. Substance use must not become victim-blaming.

Zimri's seven-day reign begins with massacre and ends when he burns the palace over himself. His death is a suicide under siege and political collapse, not a heroic model or proof that all suicidal deaths are Divine punishment.
The text immediately moralizes Zimri's death through his sins. Modern readers must not shame people with suicidal thoughts, people who die by suicide, or bereaved families.
The succession from Zimri to Omri passes through military acclamation, siege, civil division, and Tibni's death. Political stability emerges from violence, not consensus.
Samaria's founding includes a land purchase from Shemer. The transaction does not reveal the status of other residents or whether the sale transferred communal rights.

Jezebel is identified as a Sidonian princess and associated with Ahab's Baal policy, but Ahab is the ruling actor who marries, builds, serves, and establishes the cult. Her gender and foreignness must not carry his responsibility.
Baal and Asherah polemic may not justify violence against living religious communities, vandalism, or xenophobia.

The deaths of Hiel's sons at Jericho's foundation and gates may reflect curse fulfillment, construction sacrifice tradition, or compressed family tragedy. Child death must never be treated as an acceptable building cost or ritual offering.
safety_note: Do not romanticize assassination, dynastic massacre, palace self-burning, civil war, or child death. Do not blame alcohol, Jezebel's gender, Sidonian identity, or minority religion for royal violence. Handle Zimri's death with suicide-safe language and compassion.
